mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE increases by >0.3pp, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of periods when HOUST increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production growth signals supply chain constraints, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5% YoY, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and the federal funds rate is high, it indicates a tight labor market with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with high rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 35% of periods when UNRATE is low and FEDFUNDS are high, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending signals strong demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 45% of periods when RSAFS increases by >0.5% MoM, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate signals higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 30% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment signals a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when PAYEMS increases by >100k, this hypothesis is falsified.
